title: Prime coordinates of compatible families span the completed module
statement: Let $R,S$ be commutative rings, $\varphi:R\to S$ a flat map [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], $t\in\mathbf N$, and $f:\{0,\ldots,t-1\}\to R$. Put $I=(f_i)$ and assume the induced map $R/I\to S/IS$ is bijective. For any module glueing datum $X$ [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-data], let $H^0(X)$ be its module of compatible families [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-H0], and let $p(h)$ be the prime coordinate of $h$. Then the $S$-linear span of $\{p(h):h\in H^0(X)\}$ is all of $X.M\prime$.

source.place: Tag 05ER, Proposition (proposition-equivalence), canonical comparison Psi; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05ER

proof.text: Apply the existing canonical equivalence under flatness and quotient bijectivity to obtain a module M and an isomorphism Can(M) to X. Its prime component, after transport along the specified object equality, is a surjective S-linear map from S tensor_R M to X.Mprime.

For each m in M, construct the compatible tuple whose prime coordinate is 1 tensor m and whose chart coordinates are m/1. Transport along the object equalities. The compare and swap fraction formulas verify the two families of H0 equations. A morphism of glueing data preserves these equations, by evaluating its prime and chart compatibility squares at fractions with denominator 1.

Transport the preceding tuple through Can(M) to X. Its prime coordinate is the image of 1 tensor m. Tensor induction proves every image lies in the span: use zero, addition, and s tensor m = s times (1 tensor m). Surjectivity of the transported prime map proves the span is top.

theorem h0_prime_span_eq_top {R : Type u} {S : Type v}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (φ : R →+* S) (t : ℕ) (f : Fin t → R)
    (hflat : φ.Flat)
    (hquot : Function.Bijective
      (Ideal.quotientMap ((Ideal.span (Set.range f)).map φ) φ Ideal.le_comap_map))
    (X : Data.{u, v, max u v w} φ f) :
    Submodule.span S (Set.range (fun h : h0 φ f X ↦ (h.val.1 : X.M'))) = ⊤
